records.notes:
THIS IS LOG ENTRY 3. Counted ADDITIVE on Geno’s confirmation, and the frames support him: IMG_3404 faces the bridge at Crossing A (~10 geese), IMG_3405 is 9 s later FROM THE SAME SPOT BUT TURNED, facing the Asbury bank and townhouses (~9 geese), IMG_3406 is 2.5 min later and 39 m on (~5). Different water in each. Total ~24, against Entry 3’s ~26 — agreement.

CLAUDE GOT THIS WRONG FIRST. framing.py groups all three into one sighting event (9 s / 39 m apart), and Claude read that as evidence the geese were re-photographed, proposing a correction from ~26 down to 10. The event grouping is a GEOMETRIC heuristic — it says frames MAY show the same birds, never that they do. It cannot see that the photographer turned. An eyewitness who was standing there outranks it. This is the case count_basis "additive" exists for.

The largest single count in the record, by some way.
